mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI or 220 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C200 CDI or C220 CDI typically costs between £500 and £4,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM611 units start from £500-£1,200, reconditioned from £1,100-£2,200, and fully rebuilt OM651 engines from £2,500-£4,800. A replacement OM646.811 engine costs on average £1,918 in good condition, with reconditioned units costing up to £2,703. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is 'Black Death' and does it affect the C-Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: 'Black Death' refers to injector seal failure that affects OM611, OM612 and OM646 engines. The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates hard, black carbon deposits around the injector. Symptoms include a ticking or chuffing noise, a strong diesel smell in the cabin, hissing sounds from the engine, and visible black tar-like residue. If left untreated, the injector can seize in the cylinder head, requiring expensive extraction and head repairs.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the engine. The OM611 and OM646 (W203 and early W204) use a duplex timing chain at the front of the engine, which is robust and does not require scheduled replacement. The OM651 (W204 C220 CDI from 2008) uses a timing chain at the rear of the engine, which is prone to stretching. A metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI or 220 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W203 C200 CDI or C220 CDI is typically worth £1,500-£3,000 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value, making a used engine or targeted repair more economical. A W204 C200 CDI or C220 CDI is worth £3,500-£8,000 - a rebuilt OM646 or OM651 engine (£2,000-£4,800) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM611, OM646 and OM651 engines in the C-Class?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM611 is the original 2.2-litre common-rail diesel used in the W203 C200 CDI and C220 CDI (2000-2004) with a front-mounted duplex timing chain. The OM646 is a refined version of the OM611 with improved injector sealing, used in the W203 facelift and early W204 (2003-2009). The OM651 is a 2.1-litre diesel introduced in the W204 C220 CDI from 2008, featuring a rear-mounted timing chain and 2,000 bar rail pressure.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C200 CDI and C220 CDI is most commonly caused by turbocharger issues, particularly sticking variable vanes from carbon buildup. Other causes include EGR valve clogging, injector seal failure ('Black Death'), and on OM651 engines, timing chain stretch causing cam timing drift. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C200 CDI and C220 CDI badges span two generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class, representing the core diesel offerings across the W203 and W204. The C200 CDI served as the entry-level diesel, while the C220 CDI offered more power and torque. Both badges evolved through three engine families - the OM611, OM646 and OM651 - each with distinct characteristics and failure patterns.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C200 CDI and C220 CDI have been powered by three distinct diesel engine families across the W203 and W204 generations - the OM611, OM646 and OM651. The OM611 and OM646 are renowned for durability with front-mounted duplex timing chains, but all share the "Black Death" injector seal failure. The OM651 introduced a rear-mounted timing chain that became the primary replacement driver. Rebuilt C200 CDI and C220 CDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM611 / OM646 Injector Seal Failure - "Black Death" Carbon Buildup
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C200 CDI and C220 CDI (OM611.962 and OM646.963/811, W203 and W204, 2000-2009)
problems.rootCause: The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the seal. The escaping gas mixes with carbon and unburnt fuel, creating hard, black, crusty deposits around the injector. Mercedes vehicles with OM611, OM612 and OM646 engines are "particularly notorious for Black Death". Symptoms include a chuffing or ticking noise, a strong diesel smell in the cabin, hissing sounds from the engine, and visible black tar-like residue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove one injector, clean seat, replace copper washer and clamp bolt
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents injector seizure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: All four injector seals replaced, carbon removal from bores, leak-off testing
repairOptions.longevity: For moderate carbon buildup; specialist approach significantly cheaper

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seized injector drilling/extraction, cylinder head removal, injector bore machining
repairOptions.longevity: Required if injector cannot be extracted non-destructively

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W203 C220 CDI is worth £1,500-£3,000, while a W204 C220 CDI is worth £3,500-£8,000. For W203 vehicles, a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value - a used engine or targeted injector seal repair is usually more economical. For W204 vehicles in good condition, a rebuilt OM646 or OM651 with warranty can be a worthwhile investment.
problems.recommendation: The "Black Death" is insidious but slow-moving. If you hear a ticking or chuffing noise that changes with engine speed, or smell diesel fumes in the cabin, inspect the injector area immediately. Caught early, an £180-£300 single seal replacement is cheap peace of mind. On an older W203 C-Class with 120,000+ miles where an injector has seized, replacement of the whole engine sometimes makes more sense than a £1,200-£2,200 head repair.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM611 and OM646 Mercedes-Benz C200 CDI / C220 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Failure - Why the W204 C220 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a timing chain mounted at the rear of the engine, adjacent to the gearbox. The chain stretches over time due to inadequate tensioner design and extended oil change intervals. A metallic rattling or clattering noise on cold start for 2-5 seconds is the classic warning sign. If the chain jumps or snaps, the engine requires cylinder head removal and valve replacement. Some owners have reported chain failure at 90,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioners, guides, and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, valve replacement, piston inspection, full timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt OM651 unit with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold starts - especially between 80,000 and 120,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£700-£1,100) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes-Benz C220 CDI engine prices

problems.group: OM611 / OM646 Turbocharger & EGR Valve Issues
problems.h4: OM611 / OM646 Turbocharger & EGR Valve Issues
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C200 CDI and C220 CDI (OM611.962 and OM646.963/811, W203 and W204, 2000-2009)
problems.rootCause: The variable geometry turbocharger can suffer from sticking vanes due to carbon buildup, causing loss of boost and reduced power. EGR valve clogging from carbon deposits is also common, particularly on vehicles used for short journeys.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve; or replace if necessary
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; carbon buildup is the main cause

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace or rebuild turbocharger, oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo has failed or vanes are seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new turbo and EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C200 CDI or C220 CDI experiences loss of power, particularly when climbing hills, have the turbocharger and EGR system inspected. A £300-£600 EGR clean or £800-£1,500 turbo repair is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Regular motorway driving helps keep the EGR and turbo vanes clear.
